rounds.text: Unihealth Hospitals Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an EV/EBITDA of 10.05x against a sector benchmark of 16.23x and a P/E of 22.03x compared to its sector benchmark of 30.64x [E6, E11]. The business demonstrates exceptional capital efficiency, delivering a return on equity of 38.04% and a return on capital employed of 33.03%, both of which vastly outperform their respective sector benchmarks of 10.16% and 11.82% [E9, E10]. Top-line expansion has been robust, supported by compounded sales growth of 38% over 5 years and 44% over 3 years, alongside recent screen triggers highlighting year-over-year sales growth of 77% [E14, E15, E61]. This fundamental strength is captured by a rules-based screen scoring 86 out of 100 with a medium confidence buy rating, operating within a healthcare sector characterized by a strong macroeconomic tailwind score [E60, E68, E70]. Furthermore, capital expenditure appears largely completed as capital-work-in-progress is down 90.0% to Rs 1 Cr, pointing towards new capacity coming online [E35]. Conceded: free cash flow was negative at Rs -26 Cr in March 2026, cash conversion is weak at 0.13x, and debtors remain high at 341 days [E29, E31, E59].

Despite strong historical growth metrics, Unihealth Hospitals Ltd exhibits significant fundamental and structural vulnerabilities that undermine its current valuation [E1, E14]. Profit growth has experienced a sharp deceleration, with trailing twelve-month profit growth slowing to just 3% alongside contracting operating margins that show an inconsistent trend [E19, E25, E27]. Cash generation is deeply concerning, highlighted by a paltry cash conversion ratio of 0.13x for March 2026 where profits vastly outstrip operating cash flow, resulting in negative free cash flow of Rs -26 Cr and dangerously high debtor days stretching to 341 [E29, E31, E59]. Furthermore, financial risk is escalating as borrowings surged to Rs 89 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 33 Cr a year prior, accompanied by warning flags regarding suspicious accounting practices such as potential interest capitalization and low tax rates [E34, E57, E58]. Institutional abandonment is stark, with foreign and domestic institutional holdings dropping significantly since 2023, negative institutional money flow, and declining promoter stakes [E36, E37, E38, E39, E56]. Technical momentum is equally weak, with the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages and suffering from high annualized volatility of 68.8% [E45, E49]. Conceded: [E8], [E9], [E10], [E11].

While the bear points to slowing trailing twelve-month profit growth of 3% and inconsistent operating margins, it ignores historical compounding where 5-year sales and profit growth sit at an impressive 38% and 39% respectively [E14, E17, E19, E25, E27]. Conceded: [E29], [E31], [E59]. The bear highlights rising borrowings to Rs 89 Cr and potential interest capitalization flags, but fails to account for a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 5.33x alongside a moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.60x [E32, E33, E34, E58]. Concerning institutional and promoter stake reductions are real, yet they overshadow the company's elite fundamental returns, including an exceptional ROE of 38.04% and ROCE of 33.03% that vastly outperform sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E36, E37, E38, E56]. Conceded: [E45], [E49]. Finally, despite weak technical moving averages, the rules-based screen awards the company a solid 86 out of 100 buy score supported by a massive sector tailwind score and strong recent YoY sales and net profit surges [E60, E61, E63, E68, E70].

The bull leans heavily on historical 5-year sales and profit compounders of 38% and 39% [E14, E17], but glosses over the severe deceleration occurring right now, where trailing twelve-month profit growth has plummeted to a meager 3% alongside inconsistent operating margins that have slipped by 3 percentage points [E19, E25, E27]. Conceded: [E14, E17, E19, E25, E27]. While the bull dismisses rising borrowings to Rs 89 Cr by pointing to a 0.60x debt-to-equity ratio and comfortable current ratio [E32, E33, E34], it completely ignores red flags warning that the company might be capitalizing interest costs, has extreme debtor days stretching to 341, and printed a negative free cash flow of Rs -26 Cr with a dismal cash conversion ratio of 0.13x [E29, E31, E58, E59]. Conceded: [E32, E33, E34]. The bull brushes off institutional and promoter stake reductions as minor noise against elite ROE and ROCE figures [E9, E10, E36, E37, E38, E56], yet foreign institutions have nearly emptied their holdings down to 0.01% while domestic institutions cut allocations to 0.45%, generating a definitive negative institutional money flow signal [E37, E38, E39]. Conceded: [E9, E10].
